metadata.title: Train Claude on Your Best Posts
metadata.purpose: Show viewers how to extract public LinkedIn posts with Apify, upload to Cowork, generate a writing report and SOP, build a reusable /skill, and generate post angles on demand.

props.segment: Train Claude on Your Best Posts
props.command: What is: Train Claude on Your Best Posts?

beats.narration_text: Namaste. This is Liam, in for Bear. What if Claude could learn your writing voice from your best LinkedIn posts and generate new angles on demand? Here is the exact setup to make that happen.

props.ask: How do I train Claude on my LinkedIn posts to write in my voice?
props.answer_preview: Extract your public posts with Apify, upload the spreadsheet to Cowork, and...
props.command: What if Claude could learn your writing voice from your best LinkedIn posts and generate new angles on demand?

beats.narration_text: The workflow has five steps. One: use Apify to safely and legally extract up to one thousand public LinkedIn posts from any profile. Two: download the results as a spreadsheet. Three: upload the spreadsheet to Claude Cowork. Four: build a writing report and a reusable skill from the analysis. Five: use the skill whenever you need new post angles.

illustration.layout: Vertical numbered list — five steps connected by a single terracotta vertical line on the left. Each step has a short label: '1 Apify extract', '2 Download spreadsheet', '3 Upload to Cowork', '4 Build report + /skill', '5 Generate angles'. Simple flat design, no icons beyond step numbers in circles.

beats.narration_text: Go to Apify. Create a free account — there is a free tier that gives you enough credits to extract up to two thousand posts. Your LinkedIn posts are all publicly visible on the web, so this extraction is safe and legal. Download the result as a spreadsheet.

card.sub: Public LinkedIn posts → spreadsheet — safe and legal

beats.narration_text: Open Cowork. Upload the spreadsheet. Paste a prompt that asks Claude to analyze the format, hooks, and angles across all the posts. Cowork will run for several minutes — it is reading hundreds of posts. The output is a full report and an SOP: a standard operating procedure for writing posts in your voice.

card.sub: Cowork reads all posts → outputs format, hooks, angles analysis

beats.narration_text: In the same chat, continue and ask Claude to create a reusable skill from the report. The skill captures your post patterns, your hooks, your voice. Once created, you can share it with your team. Whenever you want to write a new post, invoke the skill — Claude already knows your style.

card.sub: Build /skill from the report — invoke it for every new post

beats.narration_text: Three honest limits. This only works if you post at least once a week — if you have fewer posts, there is not enough data for Claude to learn from. It does not work on bad content — Claude trains on what you give it. And it repeats patterns rather than inventing novelty. Going viral often requires something new. This tool helps you write better versions of what already works for your audience.

card.sub: Works best with consistent posters — repeats what works, not what's new

beats.narration_text: Go to Apify, create an account, and extract your last hundred LinkedIn posts. Upload the spreadsheet to Cowork. Run the analysis prompt. In one session, you will have a writing report and a reusable skill that knows your voice.

card.sub: Apify → spreadsheet → Cowork → skill. One session.

beats.narration_text: The best AI writing tool is still the one that sounds like you. Claude learns the patterns. You bring the taste. Together you stop staring at a blank page. This is Liam, in for Bear.

card.copy: TRAIN CLAUDE ON YOUR BEST POSTS
card.sub: this is Liam, in for Bear

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: you want Claude to write LinkedIn content in your voice, not its generic professional voice. Ask Claude to show you the voice-capture method: how many of your own posts to include as examples, what to annotate in them so Claude extracts your patterns rather than your topics, and how to test whether Claude's output actually sounds like you.

props.command: I want Claude to write LinkedIn content in my voice, not its generic professional voice. Show me the voice-capture method: how many of my own posts to include as examples, what to annotate in them so Claude extracts my patterns rather than just my topics, and how to test whether Claude's output actually sounds like me or just like a polished version of the platform default.
